strengths: Addresses a well-motivated and practically important problem: generating physically plausible, instance-interactive tabletop scenes for robotic manipulation data synthesis, filling a gap between room-scale generative scene methods and asset-library-limited tabletop methods (e.g., MesaTask).

The technical pipeline is clearly decomposed and each component is well justified: generative instance extraction with mask completion for occlusion handling, a Differentiable Rotation Optimizer with a sensible tri-modal loss (silhouette, edge, DINOv2 appearance), and a Top-View Spatial Alignment module with a principled RMA-Score for anchor selection that combines area and aspect-ratio consistency.

Extensive and multi-faceted evaluation: quantitative comparisons against both image-driven (ACDC, Gen3DSR, MIDI) and text-driven (MesaTask, Holodeck-table) baselines, a large-scale user study with 128 participants, GPT-4o-based multi-dimensional scoring, and thorough ablations isolating DRO and TSA contributions.

The zero-shot real-to-sim-to-real policy transfer experiment (training π0.5 purely on synthetic trajectories and deploying directly on a physical AgileX PiPER arm) is a strong and convincing piece of evidence for the practical utility of the generated data, going beyond purely visual/simulated metrics.

Physical plausibility is evaluated with meaningful, non-trivial metrics (collision rates, and in the supplementary, Support Stability and Dynamic Settling Stability), and the paper is refreshingly self-critical about potential biases in its own best-view evaluation protocol, providing a mean-view analysis to address this.

Supplementary material is unusually thorough (stage-wise intermediate outputs, prompts, additional baselines SceneGen/FlashSculptor, user-study UI details), aiding reproducibility and transparency despite reliance on proprietary components.
weaknesses: The core system is largely an orchestration of existing large pretrained models (ChatGPT/GPT-4o, Seedream, Hunyuan3D-3.0, GroundedSAM-v2), with the primary original technical content residing in the pose/scale alignment (DRO+TSA) stage; the paper should be judged as an applied/systems contribution rather than a fundamentally new algorithmic/generative technique, which somewhat limits its intrinsic novelty even though the engineering integration is solid.

Heavy dependence on closed, proprietary APIs (GPT-4o, Seedream) raises reproducibility concerns, since these models may change over time, incur ongoing cost, and are not fully controllable/inspectable by other researchers attempting to replicate results.

GPT-4o is used both implicitly in the generation pipeline (semantic reasoning, size priors, stacking relations) and as an evaluator (VF/IA/PP scoring), which introduces a degree of potential circularity/self-consistency bias in the automatic evaluation, only partially mitigated by the independent human user study.

The test set (78 scenes) and the real-to-sim-to-real validation (only 3 tasks, 50 trials each) are relatively modest in scale for claims of a general-purpose 'data engine'; more diverse manipulation tasks, object categories, and larger-scale policy training/evaluation would strengthen the impact claims.

The method is restricted to rigid objects on a single flat tabletop and does not address articulated/deformable objects or more complex support structures (shelves, drawers), which the authors acknowledge as future work but somewhat narrows current applicability.

No detailed analysis of failure cases or computational cost/latency per scene is provided, which would be useful for assessing the practicality of scaling this pipeline to generate very large synthetic datasets.
